- When sentiment turns negative or shows sharp decline (especially > -0.67 change), model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% relative to recent peak.
- After strong upward spikes (sentiment > 0.67 for 3+ days), model often overshoots — cap forecast at 1–2% below recent high or use 3-day moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment is consistently positive but trending down (e.g., -0.33 to -0.67 change), model underreacts — increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% to reflect mean reversion bias.
- When sentiment is flat or neutral (±0.33), model often lags — add 0.3–0.7% to forecast to account for delayed reaction.
- If news volume is high (3.0) and sentiment is volatile, model overfits short-term noise — apply 1–2% smoothing filter to avoid overreaction.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate late-period spikes — adjust forecast by +0.5–1.0% for days 25–30 if sentiment > 0.67 and price > 70.00.
